notes: The biennial report places the FY2024 Novva award in Clark County. The GOED board packet for the same award (identical sales and use tax figure of $20,775,423 and personal property figure of $5,764,590) describes a 300,000 sq ft facility in Storey County. The board packet is the underlying application document and is treated as authoritative.
The biennial report reuses the entity name from Novva's earlier FY2022 Clark County award. The two awards are distinct projects with distinct entities.
Apparent transcription error in the biennial report: MN11 for NV11. Vantage numbers its Nevada single-purpose entities NV11, NV12.
The FY2010-2022 report codes this award E (expansion); the FY2023-24 report codes the same award N (new). The later report is used, but neither is corroborated by a board packet.

Only the earlier figure is arithmetically consistent: $3,218,566,566 contracted less Rackspace's withdrawn $422,000,000 equals exactly $2,796,566,566. The later figure is $49,228,760 lower, which is close to but not equal to Via West's $49,278,038 capital investment (a difference of $49,278), and is unexplained by any documented withdrawal.

The Total Annual Wages column is unreliable and is excluded from this dataset. For the four FY2016 rows it equals jobs x hourly wage x 2080. For the MECP1, both Design and both Novva rows it does not: Design (Clark) implies $3,250,000 but prints $3,013,920; Novva (Clark) implies $700,128 but prints $3,013,920; MECP1 implies $2,460,640 but prints $600,704. Every fiscal-year total row prints the identical $82,767,610.

In the After Audit Results + Withdrawals rows, the sales and use tax column repeats the FY2016 post-withdrawal total ($159,387,374) instead of each year's own figure. No company withdrew in those years, so the correct value equals the contracted total shown one row above.

Within the same table, the contracted row shows $31.29 and the After Audit row shows $32.19 for the same single award. No audit had been completed for this award, so the source of the higher figure is unclear.

The GOED board packet for a March 2024 (FY2024) application states the applicable statutory wage as $29.28. The City of Reno memo labels $32.51 as the FY2024 figure. The November 2024 (FY2025) board packet also uses $32.51, which suggests $32.51 is the FY2025 figure and the Reno memo's label is off by one fiscal year.
